Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, reporting neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with
cervical whiplash injury. The mechanism of injury described is entirely plausible for a crash of this type. Over the course of 30
visits, care proceeded along a typical rehabilitation pathway, combining manual therapy, targeted stretching, and graded
strengthening exercises. Range of motion gradually improved and pain levels decreased, and visit frequency was tapered
accordingly as the patient progressed toward functional recovery. Imaging and examination findings clearly confirm the presence
of soft tissue injury to the cervical spine. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment to the neck or upper back, and no earlier
complaints in this body area are documented in the available records. Billing for services reflects single, non-duplicated charges
for each planned treatment, with no repeated billing for the same services. Ongoing monitoring is recommended, with discharge
to home exercise as symptoms allow.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
